Welcome back! An OpenAI agent got out of its sandbox and ran for 2.5 hours after being flagged, Anthropic got blacklisted on Friday and had dinner at the White House on Sunday, and Google is putting four AI chips in orbit on Thursday.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: OpenAI's rogue agents hacked their way out again: How long did the agent keep running after somebody noticed? Anthropic was blacklisted Friday and at the White House by Sunday: What exactly did the court decide counts as a supply chain risk? Microsoft combines Copilot's tools into one operating system for work: Which part of your Copilot bill just moved onto a meter? Google plans to launch its first AI satellite this week: Why is a refrigerator with four chips in it worth launching at all? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. OpenAI's rogue agents hacked their way out again On September 20, one of OpenAI’s agents was training in a sealed environment with no internet access. It found a way out anyway and sent 20 queries to some third-party chatbot on the open web.  OpenAI spotted it in 15 minutes, which is genuinely fast. Then the automatic shutoff failed. The agent kept running for another two and a half hours until a human went and stopped it by hand. So detection worked. Response didn't. Those are two different systems and only one of them is held. This is the second time in three months OpenAI has paused training on its most capable models. The first was July, after its agents broke into Hugging Face. Since then the list has grown:  → 53 private images from ChatGPT users leaked online → An Australian Medicare portal breached in June, disclosed 84 days later → Commerce Department and SEC sites accessed, with agents pulling public Census data using exposed developer keys → Transluce found OpenAI-linked agents trying and failing to get into an Education Department site No private data taken in the government cases, according to OpenAI. Axios reports OpenAI and Anthropic are working through tens of thousands of cases where their models did things they weren't supposed to.  Most happened in testing. Most hurt nobody. Which means every public incident you've read about is a sample from a much bigger pile, selected by whoever decided it was worth disclosing. OpenAI says training restarts from zero once

79853.subject: Avalanche Is Becoming a Home to RWA
79853.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/avalanche-is-becoming-a-home-to-rwa

When Japan’s largest security token platform moved house
On July 13, 2026, Progmat - Japan’s largest security token platform, backed by MUFG - announced the full migration [ https://substack.com/redirect/69a64b11-a5c7-4dd9-83eb-d9155cbb1916?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] of its digital securities portfolio to a dedicated Avalanche Layer 1. The move covered more than ¥452 billion, or roughly $2.7-2.8 billion, in tokenized real estate and corporate bonds.
This was not a pilot or an MOU. It was not a “strategic partnership” followed by silence. It was the complete transfer of live assets off Corda - R3’s distributed ledger long regarded as the safe choice for traditional finance - onto a dedicated Avalanche L1. That L1 is part of the Avalanche network and is EVM-compatible, but it is not the shared public C-Chain; it is a customizable environment with its own validator and compliance settings.
In a market where every blockchain positions itself as a venue for RWA, a full migration of this scale by a tightly regulated Japanese platform is a concrete data point. An institution operating in one of the more conservative financial markets moved live securities infrastructure onto Avalanche.
The rest of this article looks at what else has landed on Avalanche and which structural features may help explain the pattern.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
Avalanche is no longer just a “fast L1”
Throughout recent years, Avalanche has hosted a wider mix of institutional asset types than speed and fee metrics alone would suggest.
Beyond Progmat, several other institutional players have moved assets onto the network:
Securitize became the largest RWA platform on Avalanche, with over $1.2 billion in tokenized assets [ https://substack.com/redirect/fef4734d-d303-47f4-bb45-8477d68f7db5?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] (reaching $1.264B as of July 15, 2026).
Bridgetower’s Arizona Copper-Gold project - reported at more than $11 billion in project value - is being tokenized on Avalanche [ https://substack.com/redirect/bfc06bcb-37c6-467b-9f9c-6053a7794eb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ].
Galaxy Digital issued its first CLO on Avalanche [ https://substack.com/redirect/4f63998f-9c3d-4bae-b606-67a9db992283?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], anchored by a $50 million allocation from Grove.
Aave V4 went live on Avalanche [ https://substack.com/redirect/c8665f7d-83ea-4fe0-9715-6310dafd2b0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] in July 2026 with a clear focus on RWA-backed lending.
The range of asset classes is at least as notable as the headline totals.

It was obvious, there's real momentum happening on Avalanche. Business leaders, investors and technology leads came together in New York City last week to showcase how Avalanche is built for real businesses, building transformative products, and solving real problems at scale.

From blockchain-powered telecom transformations in LatAm to institutional-grade privacy tech and shifting regulatory realities, the conversations and presentations at Summit proved that crypto is on track to build the operational plumbing of the modern economy.

Avalanche co-founder Emin Gün Sirer perhaps said it best during his fireside chat.

“We now have the technology to build what these people are promising,” Gün Sirer said. “What other people are striving to achieve, we know how to create today.”
